uutiset.t: India Says US Trade Deal Nearly Ready, Signing May Take Time
uutiset.s: India and the US could conclude negotiations on a trade deal soon, though signing and implementing it may take longer, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said Wednesday.

uutiset.t: Davidson Kempner Warns of Credit Markets 'Fear Factor'
uutiset.s: As concerns mount in fixed-income markets, Chris Krishanthan, who co-manages the global credit department at Davidson Kempner, says "there’s a real fear factor that developed." He made the comments at Bloomberg's Global Credit Forum in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Crypto Futures Point to a Big Pop for Anthropic Stock
uutiset.s: Bulls on AI are driving huge demand for the IPO.

uutiset.t: Credit Chiefs Warn of ‘Fear Factor’ as Debt Reprices All at Once
uutiset.s: A sharp repricing across fixed-income markets in recent months is likely to continue as interest rates remain elevated, causing a shakeout among weaker borrowers across industries.

uutiset.t: How GTA VI Became the Most Expensive Video Game Ever Made
uutiset.s: One of the biggest entertainment releases in history.

uutiset.t: How GTA VI Became the Most Expensive Video Game Ever Made
uutiset.s: It took over a decade to make Grand Theft Auto VI. And when it’s released on November 19, it will have likely already set at least one record: the most expensive video game ever made. uutiset.t: Apollo’s Europe Head Sees Massive Finance Demand for AI, Defense
uutiset.s: Europe’s urgent need to catch up on defense, power and artificial intelligence spending means the need for investment has grown significantly even since Mario Draghi outlined an action plan for the continent, yet its capital markets have failed to keep pace.

uutiset.t: Apollo Is Focused on Investment Grade, De Giorgi Says
uutiset.s: Diego De Giorgi, partner and head of EMEA at Apollo Global Management, says the firm is focused on the global industrial renaissance and is particularly focused on investment-grade and the short end of curve. uutiset.t: Dongfeng’s First Egypt-Built Electric Car to Go On Sale in 2027
uutiset.s: The first electric car built in Egypt, an SUV designed by China’s Dongfeng Motor Corp., will go on sale in early 2027 — a potential leap forward in the Arab nation’s push to modernize transport options and boost local industry.

uutiset.t: Xi Welcomes Trump at Shenzhen Airport
uutiset.s: President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping shared a cheek-to-cheek hug in a rare airport welcome in Shenzhen. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Adults Want Kids’ Toys This Holiday Season
uutiset.s: Companies are stocking their shelves with Lego sets and plushies for the holiday season, but their target audience may be surprising. Annie Bang breaks down how adults are driving growth for the US toy industry, not kids. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Anthropic Approaches Final IPO Hurdle After Tech Stocks Churn
uutiset.s: Anthropic PBC is on the cusp of pricing potentially the biggest IPO of all time, defying days of volatility in technology stocks that threaten to weigh on the startup’s long-awaited debut.

uutiset.t: BASF’s Evonik Chase Poses Test for Potential Merz Successor
uutiset.s: BASF SE’s bid to consolidate Germany’s struggling chemicals industry with a takeover of Evonik Industries AG looks set to join the ranks of politically-charged deals taking shape across Europe this year.

uutiset.t: India Studies Investors’ Tax Proposals to Boost Equity Trading
uutiset.s: Indian revenue officials are reviewing proposals from investors and economists to raise taxes on stock derivatives while lowering levies on share trading, in a bid to curb speculative bets and encourage broader participation in the equity market, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

uutiset.t: Ex-Longview Manager to Bet on Handful of Stocks in New Fund
uutiset.s: Katie Moran has an unconventional metric for equity selection at her boutique hedge fund: the few stocks making the grade will have passed a test of their “element of delight.”
